newsitem.title: FRANCE: Banned Algerian Islamists urge unity government.
newsitem.headline: Banned Algerian Islamists urge unity government.

text.p: Exiled leaders of an Algerian Moslem fundamentalist group accused President Liamine Zeroual on Wednesday of aggravating a surge of violence in the north African nation by blaming it on those working for peace.

In a statement faxed to a news agency in Paris, the leadership-in-exile of the banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) blamed the Zeroual government itself for the bloodshed and accused it of "permanent stubbornness" in rejecting all initiatives aimed at restoring calm.
"It is so blind that it accuses all those who wish to stop the bloodshed of treason and plotting," the statement said.

Algerian trade union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda was shot dead in central Algiers on Tuesday, just hours before a booby-trapped parcel exploded in the Algerian garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital, killing one person and wounding 17.
At least 176 people have died in Algeria since January 10, the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
An estimated 60,000 people have died in the country in five years of civil strife, triggered when the authorities in 1992 cancelled a general election the FIS was poised to win.
In a televised speech last Friday, Zeroual accused unnamed foreigners of being behind Algeria's "terror and fear". He vowed to eradicate what he termed a conspiracy manipulated from abroad.

Fundamentalist groups, who want to topple the Algerian government and install an Islamic republic, frequently accuse the authorities of carrying out massacres of civilians with the dual aim of discrediting the "holy war" warriors and disguising military defeats.

The FIS leadership-in-exile, which is based in Germany, urged the authorities to free all political prisoners including several FIS officials, disarm private militias, end any political role for the Algerian army, form a government of national unity and open talks with all parties aimed at a political resolution of the strife.
It also urged the international community to renew efforts to encourage a global political solution to Algeria's woes.
